STEP 1 — design-space framing and slot selection.
Goal: choose one in-scope coupling position for behaviour x hyperbolic geometry inside the RQ-VAE Semantic ID quantizer, distinct from the obvious "popularity-weighted hyperbolic Sinkhorn cost" variant.
Constraints read from the task (scope contract): the baseline's Sinkhorn-balanced level assignment must stay the assignment rule; the mechanism's score must enter INSIDE the balanced assignment as a modified cost matrix; no argmin replacement; no ablation runs, no sweeps, no multi-seed; every constant must be derived/measured.
Candidate positions considered: (a) behaviour-weighted curved Sinkhorn cost where behaviour is a scalar weight on the Poincare distance; (b) behaviour-conditioned per-item curvature; (c) behaviour-defined latent hierarchy (depth from branching); (d) behaviour-directed CURVED RESIDUAL: move the item's point in the hyperbolic ball toward a behaviour anchor built from its directed transition neighbours, then price that moved point against the codes with a geodesic distance inside the same Sinkhorn cost matrix.
Choice: (d), because it changes WHAT point the quantizer is asked to encode (a behaviour-consistent point on a curved manifold) rather than only reweighting the same Euclidean cost, so removing behaviour or removing curvature changes the core computation, not just a scalar. Worked-out detail: hyperbolic anchor = Lorentz Einstein midpoint of popularity-adjusted directed out-neighbours (stop-grad), item point = geodesic interpolation between its own lifted point and that anchor at a data-derived fraction alpha_i (participation-ratio support strength), cost = squared Lorentz distance to the level code, scale-matched to the baseline residual scale so the baseline Sinkhorn temperature/iterations are untouched.
Open at this step: exact arccosh stability, the derivation of alpha_i and the scale constant, and the three switches.

STEP 2 — specification check, constant derivation, safeguards.
Goal: make the chosen mechanism minimally implementable and verify that no constant needs tuning, that the assignment stays the baseline's Sinkhorn, and that the three switches (behaviour on/off, geometry on/off, both on) are real.
Model: Lorentz/hyperboloid, fixed curvature kappa = -1, Minkowski inner product <x,y>_L = -x0*y0 + x.v, constraint <x,x>_L = -1; d_L(x,y) = arccosh(-<x,y>_L). Lift u_i (encoder output, dim d) by s: p_i = (cosh(s||u_i||), sinh(s||u_i||)*u_i/||u_i||). s = 1/RMS(||u_i||) measured on the first training minibatch, frozen — a measured scale, not a tuned one.
Behaviour signal: directed transition counts count_ij from the Stage-2 TRAINING sequences only (successor j after i inside each user history). Popularity-adjusted edge weight = count_ij / sqrt(pop_j) (pop_j = training-split interaction count), top-m = 8 successors per item (documented default, m << mean out-degree), normalised to w_ij. N_eff(i) = 1 / sum_j (w_ij)^2 (participation ratio = concentration of the transition behaviour).
Anchor: a_i = normalise_L( sum_j w_ij * sg(p_j) ), sg = stop-gradient, normalise_L(v) = v / sqrt(-<v,v>_L). This is the Lorentz Einstein midpoint, exact and stable (no iterative Frechet solver). Cold items (no transitions) get alpha_i = 0 and fall back to the plain lifted point.
Coupling coefficient: alpha_i = N_eff(i) / (N_eff(i) + median_j N_eff(j)) over items with >=1 transition; lies strictly in (0,1), derived from the training graph, no tuning, and alpha_i = 0 exactly reproduces the geometry-only arm.
Curved residual: h_i = exp_{p_i}( alpha_i * log_{p_i}(a_i) ) = geodesic interpolation at fraction alpha_i (behaviour moves the point along a geodesic toward the transition anchor inside the ball).
Levels: level 1 prices h_i against codebook c_1k; levels 2-3 lift the Euclidean residual rho_i^(l) into the tangent space AT h_i, x_i^(l) = exp_{h_i}(s * rho_i^(l)), and price x_i^(l) against c_lk — so the whole residual chain lives on the manifold, not beside it.
Cost matrix (this is what enters the baseline Sinkhorn): C_l[i,k] = g_l * d_L(x_i^(l), c_lk)^2, with g_l = mean_i||rho_i^(l)||^2 (baseline residual scale, measured at step 0, frozen) divided by mean_ik d_L^2 at step 0, so the cost magnitude matches the baseline's and the baseline's Sinkhorn temperature/iteration count is used unchanged. Assignment rule, uniform row/column marginals and the balancing are the baseline's verbatim; I only replace the cost matrix entries.
Commit loss becomes squared geodesic distance (curved quantization) using the same Sinkhorn soft-assignment (straight-through), so gradients reach both the codebook on the manifold and the encoder through h_i.
Switches: behaviour-off = alpha_i := 0 for all i (anchor term removed, curved cost identical); geometry-off = d_L replaced by Euclidean distance between log_0 coordinates of x_i^(l) and c_lk and the anchor computed as a plain weighted mean in tangent coordinates (behaviour residual kept, curvature removed); both-on = full.
Cost check at frozen scale: 24556 items / 24 steps = ~1023 items per step; extra work per step = gather 1023x8 Lorentz vectors, one Einstein midpoint, 3 exp/log maps per item, and arccosh on 3 x 1023 x 256 = 786k pairs. The baseline already builds the same 786k-entry cost matrices, so the overhead is one dot product plus one arccosh per entry plus ~8k map evaluations: single-digit percent of step time, well under 1.15x wall clock

overall.
Safeguards: (i) arccosh evaluated as log(s + sqrt(s^2 - 1)) with the argument clamped to >= 1 + 1e-7 and squared distance additionally floored at 0; (ii) log_{p}(a) divided by its Lorentz norm with an epsilon floor, log_{p}(p) = 0 returned exactly when the anchor collapses; (iii) x_0 of every manifold point kept positive by construction through exp map (sinh/cosh), no boundary clamp needed; (iv) stop-gradient on neighbour points prevents mutual pull-in/representation collapse from the behaviour term; (v) top-m = 8 and popularity adjustment cap the influence of hot hub items; (vi) g_l measured once at step 0 so a degenerate first batch cannot rescale the cost mid-run; (vii) code usage of level 1 is still enforced by the unchanged Sinkhorn balancing, so the curvature cannot collapse the codebook.

IDEA: bhv_geodesic_anchor_sinkhorn_v1
TITLE: Behaviour-anchored geodesic residual inside the Sinkhorn Semantic-ID assignment (Einstein-midpoint transition anchor on the Lorentz manifold)
MOTIVATION: RQ-VAE Semantic IDs are learned from item embeddings alone, so items that users actually transition between often land in unrelated code prefixes; the prefix tree then encodes embedding geometry, not recommendation behaviour, and the generative recommender has to memorise transition structure itself. This idea makes the quantizer price each item at a behaviour-consistent point on a negatively curved manifold, so directed transition neighbours are pushed toward a shared prefix by the quantizer's own balanced assignment rather than by a side loss.
NOVELTY: Not a behaviour-weighted distance and not a separate hyperbolic auxiliary loss. The behaviour signal changes the POINT that is quantized (a geodesic interpolation between the item's lifted embedding and the Lorentz Einstein midpoint of its popularity-adjusted directed successors), the curvature changes the COST that the existing balanced Sinkhorn assignment minimises (squared Lorentz distance, plus curved commit loss and a residual chain transported in the tangent space at the behaviour anchor), and the two meet in a single cost matrix. Nothing in the assignment rule, the marginals or the balancing is replaced.
CHANGE: Level-1 cost becomes g_1 * d_Lorentz(geod_interp(p_i, EinsteinMid({p_j : i->j}, w_ij), alpha_i), c_1k), and levels 2-3 price the residual lifted into the tangent space at that anchored point; all three cost matrices feed the baseline's unchanged Sinkhorn.
SPECIFICATION:
Manifold: hyperboloid with fixed curvature kappa = -1, <x,y>_L = -x0 y0 + x.v, <x,x>_L = -1, x0 > 0; d_L(x,y) = arccosh(-<x,y>_L); exp_x(v) = cosh(||v||) x + sinh(||v||) v/||v|| with ||v|| = sqrt(<v,v>_L), <x,v>_L = 0; log_x(y) = d * (y + <x,y>_L x) / ||y + <x,y>_L x||.
Step 0 (once, from training data only): build directed transition counts count_ij over Stage-2 training sequences; pop_j = training interaction count; edge weight e_ij = count_ij / sqrt(pop_j); keep top-m = 8 successors per item, normalise w_ij = e_ij / sum_j e_ij; N_eff(i) = 1 / sum_j w_ij^2; alpha_i = N_eff(i) / (N_eff(i) + median N_eff), alpha_i = 0 if item i has no transitions. Also freeze s = 1/RMS(||u_i||) and, per level, g_l = mean_i ||rho_i^(l)||^2 / mean_ik d_L^2, both measured on the first training minibatch.
Every training step: p_i = exp_0(s * u_i) (u_i = encoder output); a_i = normalise_L( sum_j w_ij * sg(p_j) ); h_i = exp_{p_i}( alpha_i * log_{p_i}(a_i) ); level-1 point x_i^(1) = h_i, code point c_1k = exp_0(t_1k) with trainable tangent parameter t_1k; C_1[i,k] = g_1 * d_L(x_i^(1), c_1k)^2; (S_1, A_1) = Sinkhorn(C_1, uniform marginals, baseline iterations and temperature); commit loss += sum_ik S_1[i,k] * g_1 * d_L^2 with straight-through hard assignment; rho_i^(2) = log_0(u_i) - soft-assigned tangent code; x_i^(2) = exp_{h_i}(s * rho_i^(2)); C_2[i,k] = g_2 * d_L(x_i^(2), c_2k)^2; same for level 3 with x_i^(3) = exp_{h_i}(s * rho_i^(3)). Reconstruction and every other baseline term unchanged.
COST: One extra gather of ~1023x8 neighbour points per step, one Einstein midpoint, ~3*1023 exp/log maps and one arccosh per cost-matrix entry on 3 x 1023 x 256 = 786k entries, on top of the cost matrices the baseline already builds: single-digit percent of step time, roughly 1.05-1.15x baseline wall clock

at 24556 items / 24 steps / 3000 epochs; graph construction is one pass over training sequences before Stage 2 and costs seconds.
HYPOTHESIS: If directed transitions carry quantisation-relevant structure that the curved metric can express, then level-1 prefixes will be far more predictable from transitions (consecutive training pairs share a level-1 code well above the no-behaviour arm) while code usage stays balanced, and Stage3 test Recall@10 will rise above 0.065 in a single run; if the anchor is noise or the curvature fights the Sinkhorn balancing, prefix agreement and Recall will both sit at the geometry-only level.
RISKS: arccosh gradient blow-up when an item point lands on its code (distance -> 0); the behaviour pull can shrink the representation if neighbour gradients are not detached; Sinkhorn's uniform column marginal actively fights the co-assignment that the anchor wants, so alpha may have to fight the balancing; many items may have tiny alpha_i and gain nothing; transporting the level-2/3 residual to the anchor tangent space could distort the residual chain and hurt reconstruction; a single seed means the effect must be large to be seen.
BEHAVIOR SIGNAL: Popularity-adjusted directed item transitions (successor counts) from user histories in the Stage-2 training split, expressed as a per-item transition anchor strength alpha_i (participation ratio of the successor distribution) and a neighbour weight vector w_i.
BEHAVIOR COMPUTATION: One pass over the training-only sequences: for each adjacent pair (i_t -> i_{t+1}) in each training history increment count_ij; divide by sqrt(training popularity of j); keep the top 8 successors; normalise; compute N_eff and alpha from the training graph; recompute the set once before Stage 2 and keep it fixed. No validation or test sequence is ever read.
LEAKAGE BOUNDARY: The transition graph, popularity counts, alpha_i, the top-m neighbour sets, the scale s and the cost scales g_l are all computed from Stage-2 training interactions only, before or at the start of training, and are fixed; the encoder and codebooks see only training items and their own current parameters; validation and test interactions are never touched by the SID construction, so test Recall@10 measures transfer to unseen interactions and unseen-item fallback (alpha = 0) is a pure manifold prior, not a test-time lookup.
HYPERBOLIC OPERATOR: Fixed negative curvature kappa = -1 on the Lorentz hyperboloid: arccosh distance d_L, exponential and logarithm maps at a point, and the geodesic-interpolation step h_i = exp_{p_i}(alpha_i * log_{p_i}(a_i)), with the Einstein midpoint a_i = normalise_L(sum_j w_ij sg(p_j)) as its target.
HYPERBOLIC LOCATION: Directly inside the quantisation step of every RQ-VAE level: the metric forms the Sinkhorn cost matrix and the commit loss, and the curved exp/log maps define the points being assigned and the residual chain between levels.
COUPLING PATH: Behaviour -> anchor -> geodesic displacement -> curved point -> Lorentz distance to code -> Sinkhorn cost matrix -> balanced assignment -> codebook and encoder gradients. Removing behaviour sets alpha = 0 and the geodesic displacement vanishes; removing curvature replaces d_L by a Euclidean distance between log_0 coordinates and the Einstein midpoint by a weighted tangent mean, which changes the same cost matrix. Both changes hit the same matrix, so neither is a side term.
COUPLING EQUATION: C_l[i,k] = g_l * d_L( exp_{h_i}(s * rho_i^(l)), c_lk )^2 wi

th h_i = exp_{p_i}( alpha_i * log_{p_i}( normalise_L( sum_j w_ij sg(p_j) ) ) ); behaviour enters through (alpha_i, w_ij), curvature through d_L, exp and log, and both meet in the single Sinkhorn cost entry C_l[i,k].
OBSERVABLES: level-1 code usage count in the balanced assignment (must stay near the reference's ~241 of 256, not collapse), three-level collision rate, the fraction of training transition pairs whose two items share a level-1 code (prefix behaviour predictability), reconstruction/commit loss scale, and Stage3 test Recall@10 against the 0.065 target.
ABLATION BEHAVIOR OFF: alpha_i := 0 for all i, so h_i = p_i and the entire cost matrix reduces to the curved metric with no transition term; identical code, no separate run.
ABLATION GEOMETRY OFF: keep alpha_i and w_ij but replace d_L with the Euclidean distance between log_0 coordinates of the points and the Einstein midpoint with a plain weighted mean in tangent coordinates at the origin; the behaviour residual survives, the curvature does not.
ABLATION BOTH ON: alpha_i from the training transition graph and the Lorentz distance/exp/log maps both active, giving C_l[i,k] = g_l * d_L(exp_{h_i}(s * rho_i^(l)), c_lk)^2 fed to the baseline Sinkhorn. This is the arm that is trained; the other two exist as code switches and are not run.
SPEC EQUATIONS: <x,y>_L = -x0 y0 + x.v; d_L(x,y) = arccosh(-<x,y>_L) computed as log(s + sqrt(s^2-1)); p_i = exp_0(s u_i); a_i = normalise_L(sum_j w_ij sg(p_j)); h_i = exp_{p_i}(alpha_i log_{p_i}(a_i)); x_i^(1) = h_i; rho_i^(1) = log_0(u_i); for l = 2,3: rho_i^(l) = rho_i^(l-1) - log_0(c_{l-1, a(i,l-1)}); x_i^(l) = exp_{h_i}(s rho_i^(l)); C_l[i,k] = g_l d_L(x_i^(l), c_lk)^2; (S_l, A_l) = Sinkhorn(C_l, uniform marginals, baseline iters/temperature); L_commit = sum_{l,i,k} S_l[i,k] g_l d_L^2(x_i^(l), c_lk); code parameters live in the tangent space at the origin, c_lk = exp_0(t_lk); w_ij = e_ij / sum_j e_ij; alpha_i = N_eff(i)/(N_eff(i) + median N_eff), N_eff(i) = 1/sum_j w_ij^2; s = 1/RMS(||u_i||); g_l = mean_i||rho_i^(l)||^2 / mean_ik d_L^2 on the first minibatch.
SPEC INPUTS OUTPUTS: Inputs: encoder embeddings u_i for the ~1023 training items of the step, the frozen transition table (w_i, alpha_i), the frozen scales s and g_l, and the trainable tangent code parameters t_lk. Outputs: three cost matrices C_l (items x 256) handed to the baseline Sinkhorn, the soft assignments S_l, the hard codes A_l per level (the Semantic IDs), the curved commit loss term, and gradients to the encoder through h_i and to the codes through c_lk.
SAFEGUARDS: arccosh argument clamped to >= 1 + 1e-7 with squared distance floored at 0 and gradient masked where the clamp is active; log_{p}(a) normalised with an epsilon-floored Lorentz norm and returned as exactly 0 when the anchor coincides with the point; all manifold points produced by exp maps so the time coordinate stays positive and finite; stop-gradient on neighbour points and top-m = 8 with popularity division so hub items cannot pull the whole space; alpha_i strictly below 1 and exactly 0 for cold items; s and g_l measured once at step 0 and frozen so a degenerate batch cannot rescale the cost mid-run; the baseline's uniform marginals and balancing are used unchanged so level-1 usage cannot collapse; a NaN guard that skips the step's quantiser update if any cost entry is non-finite.
END IDEA
